paragraphs: On Friday afternoon, Tom and Ben sat on the grass next to the school gate. They had a volleyball match on Saturday, and they were very excited. "Is your team shirt in your bag?" asked Tom. "Yes," said Ben. "It has red and white stripes." "Good," said Tom. "I will put mine in my bag tonight."

"What time does the match start?" asked Ben. "At nine o'clock," said Tom, "at the sports center across the town." "How are we going to get there?" asked Ben. "The first bus leaves at nine o'clock," said Tom, "so we will be late." "Then we will take a taxi," said Ben. "A taxi is expensive," said Tom. "Who will pay?" Coach Matt came across the field with a bag of balls.

"I will pay for the taxi," said Coach Matt. "The whole team will go together." "We will meet at the school gate at half past seven," he said. "Please come early." "Do you know the way?" asked Ben. "I have the directions on my phone," said Coach Matt. "Go straight along the big road, and turn left at the crossing." "The sports center is on the right." "Straight, left at the crossing, and the center is on the right," said Tom. "I can tell the driver." "Good memory," said Coach Matt with a smile.

"We have weekly training on Wednesday," said Ben. "It was good this week." Then Coach Matt looked at his phone and made a face. "Look at the weather for tomorrow," he said. "It will be awful, with strong wind and rain all morning." "If it rains, we will not play outside," said Coach Matt. "The teams will play indoors on the big court." "Good," said Tom. "I don't like playing in the rain."

That evening, Tom packed his sports bag at home. He put in his striped shirt, a towel, and a bottle of water. Lily came into his room and looked at the bag. "Where are you going tomorrow?" she asked. "I am going to a volleyball match," said Tom. "We will meet Coach Matt at the school gate at half past seven." He set his alarm clock for six o'clock. "I will not be late," he said.

sentences.text: On Friday afternoon, Tom and Ben sat on the grass next to the school gate.
They had a volleyball match on Saturday, and they were very excited.
"Is your team shirt in your bag?" asked Tom.
"Yes," said Ben.
"It has red and white stripes."
"Good," said Tom.
"I will put mine in my bag tonight."
"What time does the match start?" asked Ben.
"At nine o'clock," said Tom, "at the sports center across the town."
"How are we going to get there?" asked Ben.
"The first bus leaves at nine o'clock," said Tom, "so we will be late."
"Then we will take a taxi," said Ben.
"A taxi is expensive," said Tom.
"Who will pay?"
Coach Matt came across the field with a bag of balls.
"I will pay for the taxi," said Coach Matt.
"The whole team will go together."
"We will meet at the school gate at half past seven," he said.
"Please come early."
"Do you know the way?" asked Ben.
"I have the directions on my phone," said Coach Matt.
"Go straight along the big road, and turn left at the crossing."
"The sports center is on the right."
"Straight, left at the crossing, and the center is on the right," said Tom.
"I can tell the driver."
"Good memory," said Coach Matt with a smile.
"We have weekly training on Wednesday," said Ben.
"It was good this week."
Then Coach Matt looked at his phone and made a face.
"Look at the weather for tomorrow," he said.
"It will be awful, with strong wind and rain all morning."
"If it rains, we will not play outside," said Coach Matt.
"The teams will play indoors on the big court."
"Good," said Tom.
"I don't like playing in the rain."
That evening, Tom packed his sports bag at home.
He put in his striped shirt, a towel, and a bottle of water.
Lily came into his room and looked at the bag.
"Where are you going tomorrow?" she asked.
"I am going to a volleyball match," said Tom.
"We will meet Coach Matt at the school gate at half past seven."
He set his alarm clock for six o'clock.
"I will not be late," he said.
